title: Revert, don't rewrite
brief:
"add telemetry" broke production. Your instinct now might be `git reset --hard` to erase it. But this history is SHARED: pretend main is already on every teammate's machine. Resetting shared history forces everyone else to repair theirs.

`git revert <commit>` does the opposite: it adds a NEW commit that applies the exact anti-change. History stays append-only; the bad commit stays visible; the effect disappears.

Revert the telemetry commit. The docs commit on top must survive.

goals.label: The telemetry commit is reverted (not erased)

hints: The telemetry commit is one below the tip: HEAD~1.
git revert HEAD~1 creates the anti-commit. No staging needed: revert commits directly.
Read the graph afterwards: 'add telemetry' is still there, and that is the point. Revert is the shared-history-safe undo.
